# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 42 (Bi-Vb Pc42)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc42
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)

**Title (English, from literature):** Using luxurious furniture

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Āsandiparibhuñjana Sikkhāpada* ("Using luxurious furniture", Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 42) is a disciplinary rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka of the Theravāda tradition [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a nun who uses a large, high, or luxurious seat or couch (such as an *āsandi*, a deckchair or divan) commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. In her study of the Theravādin Vinaya regulations for nuns, Ute Hüsken notes that like monks, nuns are prohibited from using certain furniture items such as easy chairs or divans (*Pāc 42*) as part of general restrictions on worldly luxuries and improper personal requisites [Hüsken 1997].
In SuttaCentral's curated database, direct parallels to this rule exist in the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pācittiya 42) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pācittiya 42), as well as in other Vinaya traditions preserved in Chinese and Tibetan translations: the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 115* and *lzh-dg-bi-pm-pc115*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 164* and *lzh-mi-bi-pm-pc164*), and Mūlasarvāstivāda (*xct-mu-bi-vb-pc134* and *xct-mu-bi-pm-pc134*) lineages [SuttaCentral]. Modern English translations of the rule include that by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the text shares extensive formulaic Vinaya passages with numerous other rules in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, demonstrating the highest internal reuse with Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 90, Pācittiya 49, Pācittiya 32, and Pācittiya 91–93 [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus identifies cross-language alignments with Tibetan Vinaya literature, matching passages in the Tibetan Kangyur (*BO_K01_D0003-3_H0003-3*) and the *Prātimokṣasūtraṭīkā Vinayasamuccaya* (*BO_T08_D4106-2*) [DharmaNexus].
